_comment: P-SEC.11 — NavBharatAI Pro v3.0 builder sandbox seccomp profile. OCI/Docker-format. Default-allow with an explicit denylist of privilege-escalation / host-tampering syscalls. Apply at the container-runtime layer (see docs/SANDBOX_HARDENING.md): `--security-opt seccomp=infra/e2b/seccomp-profile.json`. A default-deny allowlist is stricter but high-maintenance for a general build sandbox (npm install / vite build touch a wide syscall surface); this denylist precisely blocks the dangerous classes called out in the roadmap (ptrace, mount, setuid family, kernel-module + reboot/swap/namespace tampering) without breaking legitimate builds.

syscalls.comment: Block debugger / cross-process memory inspection — stops a compromised preview server from reading or tampering with other processes.
Block filesystem mount manipulation — prevents remounting host paths or escaping the workspace via the mount table.
Block UID/GID changes — a non-root build process cannot escalate to another user. (Pair with a non-root container user + --cap-drop ALL.)
Block kernel-module load/unload — no code path in a build sandbox legitimately touches the kernel.
Block host-level tampering — kernel replacement, reboot, swap, system clock, and process accounting are never needed by a build.
Block the kernel keyring — avoids cross-container key material access.
Block eBPF + perf — powerful kernel-tracing primitives with a history of LPE CVEs; unused by builds.
